title: "Is This a Fast for Me?"
description: "Is This a Fast for Me?" in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Drummond of Hawthornden wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 387, “A Public Fast”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Is this a fast for me?" Thus saith the Lord our God; "A day for man to vex his soul, And feel af-flic-tion's rod?

lines: Thus saith the Lord our God;
"A day for man to vex his soul,
Oppression's yoke to burst in twain,
To dwell your kindred race among,
Shall spring your health and light;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Drummond of Hawthornden died in 1649.
credits: Words by William Drummond of Hawthornden (1585–1649), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
